profile.headline: Creative software designer and developer, and "AI whisperer".... with a flair for innovative, bold -- often colorful! -- and highly functional interfaces
profile.summary:
With over 25 years of experience in software engineering, and a strong passion for AI, I specialize in creating innovative, user-friendly solutions that stand out.  I have multiple patents for 3d CAD productivity tools, have had viral success building browser developer tools, innovative music software, and now a full suite of tools for coding with AI. 

Pre-AI portfolio (mostly video)  https://www.karmatics.com/portfolio/  
(note: this page has all the content of this section with clickable links!)

I'm currently focusing on contracting and freelance work in AI development and web technologies. I enjoy pushing the boundaries of what's possible, leveraging my technical skills to bring creative ideas to life.

Whether it's developing AI applications, designing engaging user interfaces, or exploring new tech trends, I thrive on challenges and love collaborating with others who share my enthusiasm for technology.

My invention AccuDraw, has been described a tool for 3d drawing in CAD systems, has been described as "the greatest invention in cad history" (by lots of people! see: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NRDQaOdwWDo ) and is still very popular and celebrated decades after I designed and developed it.

My browser extension, Aardvark has been described by the developers of Firebug as one of the main inspirations behind it.  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ne_B2CRBeDI

I entered the Netflix Prize machine learning contest in 2006 and rose to 8th place in the first week, using solutions that were 100% "seat of the pants"(i.e.I made them up completely from scratch with no education in the field at the time). I later wrote a viral article that described my technique.

Here you can see me as "karmatics":  https://gregstoll.com/~gregstoll/netflixprize/leaderboard20061019.html
Here is my article that was widely circulated:
https://www.karmatics.com/docs/evolution-and-wisdom-of-crowds.html
Here is Slashdot discussion of my article:
https://developers.slashdot.org/story/07/10/19/0453229/evolution-and-the-wisdom-of-crowds


Finally, here are a bunch of images from my distant past (leading up to AccuDraw)
https://www.karmatics.com/portfolio/oldImages/

Old CG images from 80s and early 90s, showing skills with B-spline surfaces, rendering, etc that was very rare for the time
https://www.karmatics.com/cg/
And a whole bunch of images showing my experimentation with AI image generation:
(yeah, I like eye candy)
https://sniplets.org/galleries/moreAIImages/ (this has links to more pages as well!)
